A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAPRIKA study. The full main text, equations, Figures 1–19, Tables 1–8, and Appendices A–K are available and can be reliably matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on task success, generalization, curriculum learning, and standard benchmarks, together with appendix ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experimental results, including the main comparisons and supplementary evaluations in Appendices I–K.

M1.justification: Trajectory generation and filtering, SFT and multi-turn RPO training, and the UCB curriculum remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices C and H.

E1.justification: The ten task groups and additional LMRL-Gym, modified Wordle, standard benchmark, and standard-bandit evaluations are retained. The expanded Battleship paragraph describes the existing variant documented in B.4.8.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including GPT-4o-mini, WildChat fine-tuning, uniform sampling, and UCB. The newly cited Battleship works are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Table 1's splits and turn limits, Section 4's training and evaluation settings, and the supplementary protocols remain unchanged. No model configuration, metric, budget, or testing procedure is revised.

E4.justification: The leave-one-out and single-group comparisons, SFT/RPO ablation, WildChat control, environment-hacking audit, standard-bandit analysis, and example trajectories retain the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same uncertainty reporting, including standard errors over three seeds in Table 2 and Figures 4, 16, and 18, and averaging over 100 trials in Appendix J.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative results are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Table 2 retains all scores and uncertainties, and Figures 2–19 retain the same plotted results.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, losses in Equations 1–3, coefficient of variation in Equation 4, UCB formulation, and Appendix H estimator are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about learning generalizable decision-making strategies from synthetic interactions and improving sampling efficiency through curriculum learning.

C2.justification: Interpretations of transfer and task efficiency, and limitations concerning base-model quality, environment hacking, task grouping, and standard-bandit generalization, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Prompt examples, data construction instructions, hyperparameters, hardware and cost disclosures, and code/data/model access statements are retained. The new B.4.8 cross-reference points to technical details already present in v3.

R1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds prior-work context for Battleship, citing Grand et al. (2024, 2025) and Rothe et al. (2016, 2017, 2018, 2019), with corresponding bibliography entries. This is a focused addition to benchmark positioning.

P1.justification: v4 expands the Battleship summary, changes several cross-reference labels from Appendix to Section, and changes the displayed author name from Ruslan to Russ Salakhutdinov. The overall narrative and section organization are preserved.

P2.justification: The expanded bibliography and Battleship prose produce limited page-layout reflow. Figures 1–19 and Tables 1–8 retain their designs, substantive captions, and ordering.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies previously absent attribution and context for Battleship in Appendix B.1 and explicitly identifies its particular variant. This modestly improves research positioning and clarity, while the methods, empirical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
